emerging.signal: A credential-stealing package slipping into 47K installs proves AI tooling's dependency chains are now prime attack surfaces — expect more targeted poisoning of LLM middleware.
Anthropic publicly telegraphing a 'dramatically smarter' internal model is a deliberate market signal — they're pre-framing the next release cycle to freeze enterprise switching decisions.
Karpathy calling out memory/personalization as quality-degrading — not enhancing — challenges the entire 'persistent memory' product direction every major lab is shipping.

consolidating.signal: Claude Code isn't competing with Cursor — it's becoming the reference architecture for how agentic coding should work, with auto mode, skills, subagents, and mobile access forming a full operating layer above the IDE.
Cursor training its own frontier model + publishing technical reports signals the IDE layer is verticalizing into model training — the 'wrapper' era is definitively over.

The conversation has fully shifted from 'can agents work' to 'why agents fail at scale' — governance, auth, memory, evaluation, and ghost token burn are the real engineering problems now, not capability.
